render.stretch: per-channel black point (background neutralization) at black_k_mad x MAD below each channel's own sky, plus ONE common window width and midtone balance (linked gain and curve)
render.why_no_absolutes_here: The absolute mtf triplet is deliberately NOT pinned. It is re-derived on every run by Siril `stat main` on the layer immediately before the stretch, so it cannot go stale when a stage changes. The block this replaces pinned absolutes measured on the STAR-FUL input stack and applied them to the starless+denoised layer: measured, that layer's medians run 3.90% lower, its channel balance is 0.60% different, and its MAD/median is ~0.012 vs the stack's ~0.034, so a '4 x MAD' black point came out 2.6x too deep. Only the scale-free fractions above are ratifiable.
render.superseded_claim: The replaced block carried why_proportional: 'low/high are a fraction of each channel's OWN median so (sky-low) keeps the linear ratio'. That was verified on (sky - low) — the numerator — which the mtf then divides by (high - low); with the width also scaling per channel the ratio cancels and the construction forces the sky to EXACTLY neutral rather than preserving the linear ratio (verified numerically: 1.000036 / 1.000001). The current construction keeps the width common, which does preserve it: measured rendered sky B/G 1.0043 against the layer's linear 1.0048.
